 KenPom is struggling to find SEC wins for Kentucky
 Jack Pilgrim 4h 0 Share Share 
 Kentucky got back on track with a 29-point win over Grambling State, using an impressive 52-29 second-half finish to distance itself from last week’s disasters vs. Kansas and Northern Arizona. Sitting at 4-1 on the year, with upcoming tests against Indiana, Wichita State, Virginia, Louisville and North Carolina before SEC play to start building a resume, the opportunities are there to earn quality victories.
 KenPom is struggling to see where those come from, however.
 Coming off that 88-59 win against the Tigers, the college basketball analytics service currently projects the Wildcats to lose two of their next three—including against the Hoosiers in Indianapolis—with another non-conference loss to North Carolina in New York City right before Christmas. They do, however, have UK beating UL in Lexington on Dec. 12, an anticipated 81-80 win for the blue and white, giving Mark Pope’s squad a 53 percent chance to survive inside Rupp Arena.
 From there, though, things get really funky in the SEC. As things stand currently, Kentucky is projected to finish 17-15 overall and just 7-11 within the league. That’s pretty awful as it is. Looking at the game-by-game odds, though, KenPom is only seeing four victories, while assuming Pope will find a way to scrape together three more. 
 “Projected record is based on cumulative probabilities of winning each game and may not equal the sum of individual game predictions,” the service states.
 That presents quite the jarring visual, at least as of Nov. 17, currently projecting wins over Ole Miss (78-77), Tennessee (78-77), South Carolina (79-72) and Arkansas (81-80)—all at home. Until further notice, there is no clear path to road victories in the SEC (Oklahoma, Missouri, Mississippi State, Texas, Ole Miss, Tennessee, Georgia, Vanderbilt, and Florida) and even a handful of home losses (LSU, Vanderbilt, Alabama, Auburn, Texas A&M). 
 That’s a potential 14-18 record and 4-14 finish in the SEC, folks.
 Again, playing KenPom’s odds, Kentucky should sneak in several more wins to get above .500 and not finish at the very bottom of the barrel in the SEC, but we all know none of this will cut it in Lexington.
 Bart Torvik is actually on the same page as KenPom, also projecting a 17-15 (7-11) record, but coming in as underdogs and likely losers in 16 of the final 27 games, including 12 of 18 in the SEC. That’d be a potential 15-17 (6-12) finish, just going game by game.
 ESPN’s Joe Lunardi isn’t that down on Kentucky—but Joey Brackets still doesn’t see the Wildcats as a threat for much of anything. They fell to a No. 8 seed in Tuesday’s Bracketology update, taking on No. 9 seed Ohio State in the first round to set up a date with No. 1 seed Duke in the Round of 32. UK was projected to earn as high as a No. 5 seed as late as mid-September, but quickly fell once the season tipped off.
 Want to know how to shut all of this up? Beat Indiana, then Wichita State, then Virginia—and so on. That’s all it takes. Just win.
